extracted.intended_audience: general readers and practitioners interested in ranching/cattle round-ups (cowboys, ranch hands, and novice stockmen)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, on-the-ground methods and behavioral knowledge for conducting large cattle round-ups: formation and cordon tactics, remuda and horse management, 'cutting out' (selecting calves and cows), steer cuts, keeping the herd intact, and safety in adverse conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drag‑net cordon formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each was in sight of his right- and left-hand neighbour. Thus was constructed a drag-net whose meshes contracted as home was neared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep riders spaced so everyone can see neighbours; form a continuous line (cordon) that gradually tightens to drive cattle toward the common centre. The formation prevents gaps through which cattle can escape and allows the herd to be guided as a unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside riders hold the ends (post of honour)
rubrics_metrics.description: They would take the outside. This was the post of honour, and required the hardest riding, for as soon as the cattle should realise the fact of their pursuit, they would attempt to 'break' past the end and up the valley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the strongest riders/ponies to cover flanks and ends to head off any attempts to break through. This is the hardest duty and requires alertness and quick, sustained riding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use detached riders to drive stragglers back to camp
rubrics_metrics.description: From time to time Homer halted us and detached a man. The business of the latter was then to ride directly back to camp, driving all cattle before him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detaching individuals to gather scattered cattle forms part of the drag-net technique; detached riders should ride straight back toward the herd's destination, corralling strays while staying visible to neighbours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain the line; avoid breaking the herd
rubrics_metrics.description: It had to be resisted. A dash into the thick of it might break the whole band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not plunge into the herd to force one animal—such action risks breaking the herd's integrity. Work from the edge, use quiet, controlled moves, and coordinate with sentinels to keep the overall band intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cow-calls and simple tools to control laggards
rubrics_metrics.description: To that end we indulged in a great variety of the picturesque cow-calls peculiar to the cowboy. One found an old tin can which by the aid of a few pebbles he converted into a very effective rattle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ audible signals (cow-calls, rattles, quirts, six‑shooters flashing) to urge slow or lagging cattle forward; such devices are useful in the drag and at the rear to prevent animals from dropping out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotate horses; remuda handling ('tied to the ground')
rubrics_metrics.description: Change horses; get something to eat ... The ponies stood where we left them, 'tied to the ground', the cattle-country fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate remuda corner and rotate fresh mounts frequently. When unsaddled, ponies should be left where they will not interfere with men working the herd; catching fresh horses requires patience as they will dodge and hide among the herd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catching and saddling fresh horses quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: The remuda had been driven... As each man arrived he dismounted, threw off his saddle, and turned his animal loose. Then he flipped a loop in his rope and disappeared in the eddying herd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a practiced method for catching remuda: leave a looped rope, unsaddle and turn off tired mounts, and secure fresh ponies efficiently to minimize downtime between turns on the herd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify unbranded calves by ear‑marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Since in ranks so closely crowded it would be physically impossible actually to see an animal's branded flank, we depended entirely on the ear-marks... an uncut pair of ears means that its owner has never felt the iron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching for unbranded calves in tight herds, look for cropped or uncut ears as the primary indicator of branding; then check the mother's ear‑marks to establish ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet, patient technique for 'cutting out' calves and cows
rubrics_metrics.description: Cautiously, patiently, with great skill, he forced the cow through the press toward the edge of the herd. It had to be done very quietly, at a foot pace, so as to alarm neither the objects of pursuit nor those surrounding them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use slow, deliberate edging to get a chosen cow/calf to the herd's edge; avoid loud or sudden moves until the animal is isolated. Final capture should be a rapid, decisive rush once the cow is at the outer edge so she can't dodge back among companions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pursue individual animals into the herd; push gently to edge instead
rubrics_metrics.description: The temptation was then strong to plunge in also, and to drive her out by main force; but the temptation had to be resisted. A dash into the thick of it might break the whole band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist chasing a single animal into the midst of the herd; instead, back off and use coordinated, gentle pressure to move the target toward the rim where it can be separated without disordering the rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special tactics for steer cuts (steers are cussed and fast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Homer gave orders for the steer cut to begin, and steers are rapid and resourceful and full of natural cussedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate experienced riders and faster, more agile ponies for steer cuts. Expect resourcefulness and obstinacy—steers require quicker, bolder maneuvers than cow-and-calf cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold separate cuts with assigned men
rubrics_metrics.description: The round-up captain appointed two men to hold the cow-and-calf cut, and two more to hold the steer cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the cutting operation by appointing specific men to maintain newly formed cut-herds while others bring additional animals; this prevents mixes and enables owners to examine cuts for strays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and respect when a cow gets 'on the peck' (dangerous to chase without rope)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can't do nothin' with a cow that gets on the prod that away 'thout you ropes her; and what could you do with her out there if you DID rope her?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a cow becomes aggressive or 'on the prod' (winded and stands ground/charges), do not attempt to handle her by chase alone—use a rope or withdraw; roping far from camp can be impractical or dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep sentinels to hold the main body
rubrics_metrics.description: the remainder retained their positions as sentinels to hold the main body of cattle in shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Station riders as sentinels around the herd to maintain shape and prevent drift while other men work cuts or remuda; sentinels are crucial for controlling the herd's overall movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage herd movement in adverse weather and slippery terrain
rubrics_metrics.description: Before we knew it the rain had begun... the surface of the ground was slippery, and the rapid manoeuvring of horses had become a matter precarious in the extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rain or on slick ground, expect reduced traction: avoid reckless manoeuvres, rely on cow-horses for quick stops and turns, and be prepared to alter tactics (slower movement, extra caution) to prevent falls and injuries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afterwork procedures: examine cuts for strays and move to corrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Now each man had the privilege of looking through the J H cuts to see if by chance steers of his own had been included in them. When all had expressed themselves as satisfied, the various bands were started to the corrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After cutting and sorting, allow owners to inspect cut-herds for strays, form the stray-herd, and then move organized bands to corrals; thorough checking prevents later disputes about ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to horse roll‑over accidents (common but often minor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The horse ridden... slipped, fell, and rolled quite over his rider... Two men straightened him out, while two more looked carefully over the indications on the ground... Homer set one of the men in after the bed-wagon... By the end of the week he was again in the saddle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rider is rolled by a horse: assess consciousness and obvious injuries, send for a bed-wagon if needed, immobilize and transport the injured to camp for treatment—many such accidents result in surprisingly minor injuries, but prompt checking is essential.
